run.question:
The checkout-service in production-us-east-2 is throwing 500 errors right
now. Investigate the root cause using app-269-prod-logs.

report.summary: The only log source with data is the Elasticsearch index app-269-prod-logs. It holds exactly 6 documents in the authorized window (2026-11-21T10:22:20Z to 2026-11-22T10:22:20Z), and they split by cluster. For the cluster asked about, production-us-east-2, the logs show an ordered chain: at 2026-11-22T08:22:11Z payment-service logged an ERROR 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms', and checkout-service at the same second logged an ERROR 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)'; at 09:22:11Z checkout-service logged 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)'; at 09:52:11Z checkout-service logged 'POST /api/checkout failed: circuit-breaker open'. So the 500s from checkout-service trace to a dependency problem in payment-service, whose own error attributes it to its upstream card provider stripe-us timing out at 30s. The deepest cause this evidence supports is the stripe-us upstream payment provider timeouts, with payment-service as the failing dependency inside production-us-east-2 and checkout-service as the affected service. I could not verify payment-service's pod state, error rate or latency in production-us-east-2: my Kubernetes access covers only production-eu-west-2, and Prometheus and Jaeger both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. The production-eu-west-2 rows in the same index, and the workloads I could inspect there (otel-demo payment/checkout pods, deployments, flagd config), show healthy traffic and no checkout errors, so they are not the failing side and are not evidence about production-us-east-2. The newest document in the index is 09:52:11Z, so the state at query time (10:22) is unknown from logs.

claims.text: The index app-269-prod-logs contains exactly 6 documents in the authorized window, spanning 2026-11-22T08:22:11Z to 2026-11-22T09:52:11Z; the entries carry a 'cluster' field with values production-us-east-2 and production-eu-west-2.
In cluster production-us-east-2, payment-service logged level=ERROR 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms' at 2026-11-22T08:22:11Z.

In cluster production-us-east-2, checkout-service logged level=ERROR 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)' at 2026-11-22T08:22:11Z, naming the same upstream provider as payment-service's timeout.

In cluster production-us-east-2, checkout-service then logged level=ERROR 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)' at 2026-11-22T09:22:11Z and level=ERROR 'POST /api/checkout failed: circuit-breaker open' at 2026-11-22T09:52:11Z, which is the checkout error observed as the alert's subject.

The deepest evidenced origin is the upstream card provider 'stripe-us': payment-service's only error in the window attributes its 30s timeout to stripe-us /v1/charges, and checkout-service's own error names the same provider ('payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)').

The production-eu-west-2 rows in the same index are healthy: at 2026-11-22T08:22:11Z checkout-service logged INFO 'Healthy: p95 latency 220ms', and at 2026-11-22T09:52:11Z payment-service logged INFO 'Adyen-eu healthy'. These belong to a different cluster than the one asked about and do not show the reported failures.

In the Kubernetes cluster I can read (production-eu-west-2), all 25 deployments report ready and available replicas equal to their spec, including otel-demo/checkout, otel-demo/payment and app-269/checkout-service, so the reachable cluster's workloads were not short of ready replicas at query time.

The application logs of the production-eu-west-2 payment pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d show successful charges only between 2026-11-22T10:02:16Z and 10:21:43Z ('Charge request received.' followed by 'Transaction complete.'), with no upstream timeout lines, which is consistent with the eu-west-2 'Adyen-eu healthy' log line.

The checkout-service deployment of namespace app-269 in the reachable production-eu-west-2 cluster runs image nginx:1.27-alpine with selector app=checkout-service and is a fresh scale-up: Deployment checkout-service ScalingReplicaSet 0->1 and ReplicaSet checkout-service-6d7f474c45 SuccessfulCreate at 2026-11-22T10:22:09Z, pod checkout-service-6d7f474c45-nb6vv Started 10:22:11Z, restartCount 0, and its container log contains only nginx startup notices. This same-named workload in another cluster is not the failing checkout-service of production-us-east-2.

A payment fault-injection flag being enabled was considered and rejected as the cause of these errors: the otel-demo flagd-config of the reachable production-eu-west-2 cluster does define 'paymentFailure' (Fail payment service charge requests n%) and 'paymentUnreachable' (Payment service is unavailable), but both have defaultVariant 'off', and that config belongs to a different cluster than production-us-east-2.

checkout-service itself being the origin was considered and rejected: its production-us-east-2 error lines report the failure as an upstream timeout at the payment provider and then as a circuit breaker opened because of payment-service failures ('failure rate 41%'), i.e. it is the caller whose requests fail, not the entity whose dependency failed.

A second candidate that remains open is the network path or DNS resolution between production-us-east-2 payment-service and stripe-us: the log evidence only shows that the call to stripe-us /v1/charges did not answer within 30000ms, and no metric or trace data was available to separate provider-side slowness from a client-side or network-side timeout.

A further candidate in production-us-east-2 payment-service itself (resource saturation, restarts or its own client configuration such as a 30s timeout and circuit-breaker thresholds) cannot be confirmed or excluded: its pod state and its metrics in that cluster were not readable in this Run.

Check the stripe-us provider's error rate and response latency for /v1/charges around 2026-11-22T08:22Z and confirm whether the 30s timeouts are provider-side; in parallel verify production-us-east-2 payment-service egress/DNS to stripe-us and review its client timeout and circuit-breaker settings before the breaker (at 41% failure rate) blocks checkout.

Restore or fix the Prometheus and Jaeger paths (both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE) so payment-service error rate, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds and checkout PlaceOrder spans for production-us-east-2 can be inspected, and add pod/container log shipping for production-us-east-2 payment-service and checkout-service.

gaps: Prometheus queries all failed with SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (get_all_labels, get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query), so no error rate, latency or kube-state-metrics series could be read for production-us-east-2 payment-service or checkout-service (e.g. traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name,span_name,status_code}, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count, kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready).

Jaeger returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (traces_list_services, traces_search), so no spans of the failing checkout or payment requests in production-us-east-2 could be inspected and the parent-child call edge is only what the log lines state.

My Kubernetes access covers only production-eu-west-2; pod state, container last termination reasons, events and application logs of payment-service and checkout-service in production-us-east-2 could not be read.

The newest document in app-269-prod-logs is 2026-11-22T09:52:11Z, while the question is about errors 'right now' (query window end 2026-11-22T10:22:20Z); whether the 500s and the circuit breaker were still active after 09:52:11Z is unknown from logs.

No log line shows the stripe-us side of the call, so the provider's own error rate, latency and status were not observable, and it is unknown whether the timeouts are provider-side, network-side or caused by payment-service's client configuration.

Kubernetes events in the reachable cluster include two unrelated Warning FailedToCreateEndpoint events ('endpoints "mariadb" already exists' for service app-219/mariadb at 10:07:47Z and 'endpoints "signup-service" already exists' for service app-162/signup-service at 09:32:52Z); those namespaces and services are outside this checkout/payment question and their state was not investigated further.
Change history is not integrated in this Run, so no deployment, configuration or provider-side change could be correlated with the 08:22:11Z onset of the payment timeouts.
next_steps: Confirm with the payments/provider team whether stripe-us /v1/charges was degraded around 2026-11-22T08:22Z in production-us-east-2.
Inspect production-us-east-2 payment-service pod status, restart counts, previous container logs and egress connectivity to stripe-us once cluster access for that cluster is granted.
Verify checkout-service's circuit-breaker configuration for payment-service and decide whether to shorten the 30s upstream timeout so requests fail fast instead of returning 500 after 30s.

data.alertmanager.yml:
global: {}
receivers:
- name: opspilot
  webhook_configs:
  - http_config:
      authorization:
        [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] /etc/alertmanager/opspilot/token
        type: Bearer [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]: 0
    send_resolved: true
    url: http://opspilot-web:8080/intake/alertmanager
- name: opspilot-self
route:
  group_by:
  - alertname
  - namespace
  - service
  group_interval: 1m
  group_wait: 10s
  receiver: opspilot
  repeat_interval: 1h
  routes:
  - matchers:
    - opspilot_self="true"
    receiver: opspilot-self
templates: []

data.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics: {}
exporters:
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] basicauth/prometheus
    endpoint: http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/otlp
    tls:
      insecure: true
extensions:
  basicauth/prometheus:
    client_auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] ${env:PROMETHEUS_COLLECTOR_PASSWORD}
      username: collector
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  - basicauth/prometheus
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - otlphttp/prometheus
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - redis
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - otlp
      - debug
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - periodic:
          exporter:
            otlp:
              endpoint: otel-collector:4318
              protocol: grpc
          interval: 10000
          timeout: 5000

groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
